interviewerLines.start: Let's start the test. Here's your card.
interviewerLines.silentReading: First, please read the passage silently for 20 seconds.
interviewerLines.q1: Now, I'll ask you five questions. Please look at the passage.
interviewerLines.q2: Now, please look at the people in Picture A. They are doing different things. Tell me as much as you can about what they are doing.
interviewerLines.q3: Now, look at the {subject} in Picture B. Please describe the situation.
interviewerLines.turnOver: Now, please turn the card over.
interviewerLines.end: This is the end of the test. Could I have the card back, please?

reading: タイトルから読み始めているか
意味のまとまりで区切れているか
語の読み飛ばし・読み足しがないか

本文の該当箇所を使えているか

sets.title: Online Cooking Classes
sets.passage: These days, many people want to learn how to cook at home. Some cooking schools offer classes on the Internet, and students can join these classes from their own kitchens. In this way, people can learn new recipes without going out. Such classes are becoming more popular.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how can people learn new recipes without going out?
modelAnswer: By joining cooking classes on the Internet from their own kitchens.
A woman is washing vegetables.
A man is cutting a carrot.
A girl is taking cookies out of the oven.
A boy is wiping the table.
A woman is pouring water into a pot.
extraCheckPoints: カウンターを the table と呼んでも the counter と呼んでも正解とする

questions.subject: woman
modelAnswer: She is holding a big pot with both hands, so she can't open the door.

questions.prompt: Some people say that cooking at home is better than eating at restaurants. What do you think about that?
modelAnswer: I agree. Cooking at home is cheaper than eating out. Also, I can choose healthy food by myself.

questions.prompt: Today, many people watch videos on the Internet to learn new things. Do you often watch videos to learn something?
modelAnswer: Yes. I often watch English videos after dinner. They help me understand natural pronunciation.

sets.title: Sharing Umbrellas
sets.passage: Sudden rain can be a problem for people who do not have umbrellas. Now, some train stations have umbrella-sharing services. People can borrow an umbrella at one station and return it at another one. By doing so, they can avoid buying new umbrellas. Such services are useful on rainy days.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how can people avoid buying new umbrellas?
modelAnswer: By borrowing an umbrella at one station and returning it at another one.
A woman is buying a ticket.
A man is carrying a suitcase.
A girl is reading a book on a bench.
A boy is throwing a can into a trash can.
A woman is closing her umbrella.
extraCheckPoints: carrying / pulling a suitcase はどちらも正解とする
券売機の人物は a woman / a girl のどちらでもよい
傘の女性は closing / holding her umbrella のどちらでも正解とする

questions.subject: man
modelAnswer: His umbrella is broken, so he can't go out in the rain.

questions.prompt: Some people say that people should use trains and buses more often. What do you think about that?
modelAnswer: I agree. Trains and buses are better for the environment than cars. Also, we can read or study while we travel.

questions.prompt: Today, many people check the weather on their smartphones. Do you check the weather every morning?
modelAnswer: Yes. I check it before I leave home. I want to know if I need an umbrella.

sets.title: Visiting Farms
sets.passage: In Japan, some farmers welcome visitors to their farms. Visitors can pick fresh vegetables and learn how food is grown. In this way, children can understand the importance of farming. These programs are popular with families, and the number of such farms is increasing every year.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how can children understand the importance of farming?
modelAnswer: By picking fresh vegetables and learning how food is grown.
A man is carrying a box of tomatoes.
A woman is watering the plants.
A girl is picking strawberries.
A boy is feeding the chickens.
A woman is digging the ground with a shovel.

questions.subject: woman
modelAnswer: She wants to take a picture of the flowers, but she can't because taking pictures is not allowed.

questions.prompt: Some people say that schools should give students more chances to learn outside the classroom. What do you think about that?
modelAnswer: I agree. Students can learn things they cannot learn from textbooks. For example, visiting a farm teaches us where our food comes from.

questions.prompt: Today, many people enjoy outdoor activities. Do you often spend time outdoors on weekends?
modelAnswer: No. I usually stay home and study. I get tired after a long week at school.

sets.title: Libraries Today
sets.passage: Many libraries in Japan are changing. Some of them hold events such as reading parties and small concerts for local people. In this way, libraries are becoming places where people can meet each other. Many libraries also have cafés, and they are popular with young people.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how are libraries becoming places where people can meet each other?
modelAnswer: By holding events such as reading parties and small concerts for local people.
A woman is reading a newspaper.
A man is carrying a lot of books.
A girl is writing in a notebook.
A boy is using a computer.
A woman is drinking coffee.
extraCheckPoints: studying / writing / doing her homework はいずれも正解とする

questions.subject: woman
modelAnswer: The book is on a high shelf, so she can't reach it.

questions.prompt: Some people say that reading paper books is better than reading on a smartphone. What do you think about that?
modelAnswer: I disagree. Smartphones let us carry many books at the same time. We can also read in a dark room.

questions.prompt: Today, many students study in libraries or cafés. Do you often study outside your home?
modelAnswer: Yes. I study at the city library on Sundays. It is quiet, so I can concentrate.

sets.title: Student Volunteer Guides
sets.passage: Japan is popular with tourists from abroad. Some high school students volunteer as guides and show visitors around their towns in English. In this way, they can improve their English and learn more about their own culture. Such programs are increasing in many cities.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how can some high school students improve their English and learn more about their own culture?
modelAnswer: By volunteering as guides and showing visitors around their towns in English.
A man is taking a picture with a camera.
A woman is looking at a map.
A girl is eating ice cream.
A boy is riding a bicycle.
A woman is sweeping the street.
extraCheckPoints: 男性が何を撮っているかは言わなくてよい
sweeping / cleaning the street はどちらも正解とする

questions.subject: woman
modelAnswer: She wants to go into the museum, but the line is too long.

questions.prompt: Some people say that high school students should do more volunteer work. What do you think about that?
modelAnswer: I agree. Volunteer work helps students meet many kinds of people. It also teaches them how to work in a team.

questions.prompt: Today, many people use English on the Internet. Do you often use English outside school?
modelAnswer: Yes. I read English comments on video sites. Sometimes I write short replies in English, too.

sets.title: Secondhand Clothes
sets.passage: Many young people like fashion, but new clothes are often expensive. These days, some stores buy used clothes and sell them at low prices. Many students shop at such stores. In this way, they can enjoy fashion without spending much money. These stores are also good for the environment.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how can many students enjoy fashion without spending much money?
modelAnswer: By shopping at stores that sell used clothes at low prices.
A woman is looking in the mirror.
A man is folding T-shirts.
A girl is trying on a hat.
A boy is tying his shoes.
A woman is carrying shopping bags.
extraCheckPoints: looking in the mirror / holding a dress はどちらも正解とする
trying on / putting on a hat はどちらも正解とする
tying his shoes / tying his shoelaces はどちらも正解とする

questions.subject: man
modelAnswer: He wants to buy the jacket, but it is too small for him.

questions.prompt: Some people say that young people spend too much money on clothes. What do you think about that?
modelAnswer: I agree. Many young people buy new clothes every season. They should save money for more important things.
I disagree. Many young people buy cheap clothes at secondhand stores. They are careful about how they use their money.

questions.prompt: Today, many people buy things on the Internet. Do you often shop online?
modelAnswer: Yes. (Please tell me more.) I often buy books and clothes online. It is easy to compare prices on the Internet.
No. (Why not?) I like to see things with my own eyes before I buy them. I usually go shopping with my friends.

sets.title: Exercise Machines in Parks
sets.passage: Many people want to stay healthy, but going to a gym can be expensive. Now, some cities have put simple exercise machines in parks. Local people can use these machines for free. By doing so, they can exercise every day without spending money. Such parks are popular with elderly people.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how can local people exercise every day without spending money?
modelAnswer: By using simple exercise machines in parks for free.
A man is jogging.
A woman is walking a dog.
A boy is kicking a ball.
A girl is drinking water.
A woman is stretching.
extraCheckPoints: jogging / running はどちらも正解とする
stretching / doing exercises はどちらも正解とする

questions.subject: woman
modelAnswer: She wants to play tennis, but it is raining.

questions.prompt: Some people say that schools should have more P.E. classes. What do you think about that?
modelAnswer: I agree. Many students do not get enough exercise these days. P.E. classes are also a good way to relieve stress.
I disagree. Students need more time to study other subjects. They can exercise in club activities after school.

questions.prompt: Today, many people exercise to stay healthy. Do you do any exercise outside school?
modelAnswer: Yes. (Please tell me more.) I go jogging near my house every morning. It helps me feel refreshed before school.
No. (Why not?) I am too busy with homework and club activities. I get enough exercise at school.

sets.title: Paying with Smartphones
sets.passage: In Japan, more and more people are paying without cash. At many shops, customers can pay just by holding their smartphones over a small machine. In this way, they can pay quickly without carrying coins. However, some people still feel safer using cash, especially elderly people.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how can customers pay quickly without carrying coins?
modelAnswer: By holding their smartphones over a small machine.
A man is carrying a tray.
A woman is paying with her smartphone.
A girl is drinking juice.
A boy is eating noodles.
A man is cleaning the floor.
extraCheckPoints: paying with her smartphone が出てこなければ using her smartphone でもよい
cleaning / mopping the floor はどちらも正解とする

questions.subject: woman
modelAnswer: She wants to pay with her smartphone, but its battery is dead.

questions.prompt: Some people say that children should learn how to use money wisely at school. What do you think about that?
modelAnswer: I agree. Many young people pay with smartphones, so they do not notice how much they spend. Learning about money at school will help them in the future.
I disagree. Children can learn about money from their parents at home. Schools should spend more time on other subjects.

questions.prompt: Today, many people go to shopping malls on weekends. Do you often go to shopping malls?
modelAnswer: Yes. (Please tell me more.) I often go to a shopping mall near the station with my friends. We enjoy eating at the food court.
No. (Why not?) Shopping malls are always crowded on weekends. I prefer to stay home and relax.

sets.title: Delivery Boxes
sets.passage: Online shopping has become popular, and delivery workers are busier than before. Now, many apartment buildings have delivery boxes near their entrances. Workers can leave packages in these boxes when people are not at home. By doing so, workers can save time. People can also get their packages anytime.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how can delivery workers save time?
modelAnswer: By leaving packages in delivery boxes when people are not at home.
A woman is washing a car.
A man is carrying a box.
A girl is jumping rope.
A boy is riding a skateboard.
A man is taking out the garbage.
extraCheckPoints: 配達員は a man / a delivery worker のどちらで言ってもよい
taking out the garbage / putting a garbage bag ... はどちらも正解とする

questions.subject: man
modelAnswer: The box is too heavy, so he can't carry it.

questions.prompt: Some people say that shopping online is better than shopping at stores. What do you think about that?
modelAnswer: I agree. People can shop online at any time of day. They do not have to carry heavy things home.
I disagree. At stores, people can see and touch things before they buy them. They can also ask store staff for advice.

questions.prompt: Today, many people live in apartments in big cities. Would you like to live in a big city in the future?
modelAnswer: Yes. (Please tell me more.) There are many shops and restaurants in big cities. I also think it is easy to find a good job there.
No. (Why not?) Big cities are too crowded and noisy for me. I want to live in a quiet place with a lot of nature.

sets.title: Community Buses
sets.passage: In some areas of Japan, there are not many trains or buses. This is a problem for elderly people who cannot drive. Now, some towns run small buses that stop near people's homes. In this way, elderly people can go shopping and visit hospitals easily. Such buses are becoming more common.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how can elderly people go shopping and visit hospitals easily?
modelAnswer: By taking small buses that stop near their homes.
A woman is getting off the bus.
A man is carrying a bag of rice.
A girl is waving her hand.
A boy is picking up a cap.
A woman is putting a letter into the mailbox.
extraCheckPoints: 米の袋は a bag / a sack のどちらでもよい
putting a letter into the mailbox / mailing a letter はどちらも正解とする

questions.subject: woman
modelAnswer: She wants to take the bus, but it has just left.

questions.prompt: Some people say that it is better to live in a small town than in a big city. What do you think about that?
modelAnswer: I agree. People in small towns often know their neighbors well. They can also enjoy a quiet life in nature.
I disagree. It is not easy to go shopping or see a doctor in small towns. There are also not many jobs there.

questions.prompt: Today, many people take buses to get around their towns. Do you often take a bus?
modelAnswer: Yes. (Please tell me more.) I take a bus to the station every day. It is convenient because the bus stop is near my house.
No. (Why not?) I usually ride a bicycle to school. It is cheaper and faster than taking a bus.
